```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, error = TRUE,
  fig.align = "center", fig.retina = 2,
  fig.width = 9.7,
  fig.path = "figures/"
)
# Sum-to-zero contrasts give valid Type-III SS for unbalanced factorial ANOVA.
# Set globally so every aov / lm / lmer in the document uses the same coding.
options(scipen = 999, digits = 4,
        contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
```

> **Pipeline scope.** Pre-registered tests for H1–H5, mechanism analyses (mediation, moderated mediation, MANOVA on trust subscales), and robustness machinery (Bayesian replication, specification curve, equivalence testing, exclusion-based sensitivity, belief revision). All primary models adjust for `suspicion` (continuous, 1–6) as the sole pre-registered covariate. `offScriptPct` (binary LLM-compliance coding) was not undertaken for this dataset; specifications and sensitivity regimes that would use it are reported as not estimable.

## Analysis config — central definitions for dataset-specific constants

All dataset-specific constants are defined here, so chunks below contain no hard-coded values. The health check in §1f validates that the data matches what the config expects before any inferential chunk runs.

```{r analysis-config}
analysis_config <- list(

  # Data 
  data_path = "prolific_192_anon.csv",

  # Negotiation structure
  # Drives finalDemand, demandSlope, dataLong, round-by-round mediation,
  # demand trajectory plot, spec curve outcomes, etc.
  n_rounds = 5L,

  # Factor-level expectations after str_to_title in §1b
  label_levels        = c("Human", "AI"),
  transparency_levels = c("Opaque", "Transparent"),

  # Suspicion-probe string map
  # Must match the oTree page choice labels VERBATIM. Any mismatch
  # silently produces NAs across the board — health check (§1f) catches.
  suspicion_map = c(
    "Definitely human"  = 1,
    "Very likely human" = 2,
    "Probably human"    = 3,
    "Probably AI"       = 4,
    "Very likely AI"    = 5,
    "Definitely AI"     = 6
  ),

  # Manipulation-recall regex patterns
  # Case-insensitive substring match against the participant's recall
  # response. Each must be a unique substring of the correct option label.
  manip_label_pattern_human = "A partnerships associate from Volo Technologies (Taylor Goodenoch)",
  manip_label_pattern_ai    = "An AI negotiation agent from Volo Technologies",
  manip_trans_pattern_yes   = "Yes, I saw a transparency disclosure",
  manip_trans_pattern_no    = "No, I was not shown any disclosure",
  manip_dont_remember       = "I don't remember",

  # Demographics 
  gender_categories = c("Female", "Male", "Other", "Prefer not to say"),

  # Likert scale upper bound (drives axis limits on Mayer-scale plots)
  trust_scale_max = 5L,

  # Chat parsing 
  # The string oTree uses to flag the participant's own messages.
  chat_sender_participant = "you",

  # Pre-registered covariate strategy 
  covariates             = c("suspicion"),
  covariate_min_nonNA    = 10L,
  covariate_min_distinct = 2L,

  # SEM / bootstrap 
  bootstrap_reps = 5000L,
  seed           = 2026L,
  med_min_nonNA  = 30L,    # min non-NA needed to attempt mediation

  # Robustness thresholds (spec curve & exclusion sensitivity) 
  susp_exclusion_cutoff      = 4,    # exclude rows with suspicion >= this
  offscript_exclusion_cutoff = 0.10, # exclude rows with offScriptPct >= this

  # Equivalence testing SESOIs 
  sesoi_h1_d = 0.40,
  sesoi_h3_d = 0.30,

 # H5 mechanism profile predictions on z-scale (AI − Human)
  # Pre-registered theoretical predictions (see pre-registration, H5).
  #
  # Theoretical grounding for profile shapes:
  #   Algorithm aversion (Dietvorst et al., 2015): blanket distrust across
  #     all dimensions. Magnitude -0.5 per subscale derived from Schilke &
  #     Reimann (2025) meta-analytic θ=0.81 halved for between-subjects
  #     bilateral paradigm, distributed uniformly across three subscales.
  #   Reactance (Brehm, 1966): hostility toward the source of control. The
  #     benevolence-specific shape (competence/predictability preserved) is a
  #     theory-motivated INFERENCE, not Brehm's claim — tested, not assumed.
  #     -0.7 reflects a concentrated single-dimension effect.
  #   Strategic exploitation (Weirup et al., 2025; Rees et al., 2019): ethical
  #     fading toward AI counterparts increases selfish/misrepresenting conduct
  #     without a trust differential. Flat zero profile predicts the label effect
  #     surfaces in demands, not trust. (Castelo 2019 shows trust–behaviour convergence; the dissociation prediction follows Weirup et al. 2025.)
  #
  # The Mahalanobis distance test compares SHAPE, not magnitude. The
  # ranking is robust to small changes in specific values (±0.15).
  mechanism_profiles = tibble::tribble(
    ~mechanism,                ~competence, ~benevolence, ~predictability,
    "Algorithm aversion",            -0.5,         -0.5,            -0.5,
    "Reactance",                      0.0,         -0.7,             0.0,
    "Strategic exploitation",         0.0,          0.0,             0.0
  )
)

cfg <- analysis_config   # short alias used downstream
```

## Helpers

```{r helpers}
sigStars <- function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  if (p < .001) return("***");  if (p < .01) return("**")
  if (p < .05)  return("*");    return(" ns")
}

formatP <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  if (is.na(p)) return(NA_character_)
  if (p < .001) return("< .001")
  sub("^0", "", format(round(p, digits), nsmall = digits))
}

roundDF <- function(df, digits = 2)
  df %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, digits)))

# Figure text for use — prints Title / Subtitle / Caption below the rendered figure. 
# Keeps titling off the image itself (pair with labs(title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) in each figure).
figText <- function(title, subtitle = NULL, caption = NULL) { 
  cat("Title:    ", title, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(subtitle)) cat("Subtitle: ", subtitle, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(caption))  cat("Caption:  ", caption,  "\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n")
}

nCores <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)

# Pre-registered covariate strategy 
# Add covariates listed in cfg$covariates whenever they have variance.
# The pre-registration argues against exclusion (cell imbalance) and for adjustment.
# This single helper enforces the policy across every primary model.
addCovariates <- function(formula, df,
                          candidates = cfg$covariates,
                          min_nonNA  = cfg$covariate_min_nonNA,
                          min_dist   = cfg$covariate_min_distinct) {
  use <- candidates[
    candidates %in% names(df) &
    vapply(candidates, \(v)
           v %in% names(df) &&
           sum(!is.na(df[[v]])) >= min_nonNA &&
           length(unique(na.omit(df[[v]]))) >= min_dist,
           logical(1))
  ]
  if (!length(use)) return(formula)
  # Build candidate formula and check for aliasing before committing.
  # With small N, a covariate can become a near-linear combination of the factors, producing aliased coefficients that crash Type-III SS.
  rhs <- paste(c(deparse(formula[[3]]), use), collapse = " + ")
  candidateFormula <- reformulate(rhs, response = as.character(formula[[2]]))
  testFit <- tryCatch(lm(candidateFormula, data = df), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(testFit)) return(formula)
  aliased <- names(which(is.na(coef(testFit))))
  if (length(aliased)) {
    # Drop any covariate that caused aliasing and retry
    drop <- intersect(use, aliased)
    if (length(drop)) {
      message("addCovariates: dropping aliased covariate(s): ",
              paste(drop, collapse = ", "))
      use <- setdiff(use, drop)
    }
    if (!length(use)) return(formula)
    rhs <- paste(c(deparse(formula[[3]]), use), collapse = " + ")
    return(reformulate(rhs, response = as.character(formula[[2]])))
  }
  candidateFormula
}

# Type-III ANOVA tidier — works on aov / lm objects, returns a flat tibble
tidyAnova3 <- function(model) {
  a <- car::Anova(model, type = 3)
  e <- effectsize::eta_squared(model, partial = TRUE, ci = .95) %>% as_tibble()
  tibble(term = rownames(a),
         SS   = a$`Sum Sq`,
         df   = a$Df,
         F    = a$`F value`,
         p    = a$`Pr(>F)`) %>%
    filter(!term %in% c("(Intercept)", "Residuals")) %>%
    left_join(e %>% select(term = Parameter,
                           eta2p = Eta2_partial,
                           ci_lo = CI_low,
                           ci_hi = CI_high),
              by = "term")
}

# DATA HEALTH CHECK
# Validates that the loaded data matches what cfg expects. Called at §1f, before any inferential chunk.
# Reports FATAL issues (will produce wrong results or knit failure) and
# WARNINGS (degraded but not fatal) — never throws, so the knit continues
# and all problems surface together rather than one error at a time.

healthCheck <- function(data, cfg) {
  issues <- character(); warns <- character()
  add_issue <- function(msg) issues[[length(issues) + 1L]] <<- msg
  add_warn  <- function(msg) warns[[length(warns) + 1L]]   <<- msg

 # 1. Suspicion-string map. Empty strings are blank submissions
  # (incompleters); they should produce NA, not be flagged as a config mismatch.
  if ("suspicionRaw" %in% names(data) && any(!is.na(data$suspicionRaw))) {
    rawLevels <- sort(unique(na.omit(data$suspicionRaw)))
    rawLevels <- rawLevels[rawLevels != ""]    # treat "" as missingness
    expected  <- names(cfg$suspicion_map)
    unmatched <- setdiff(rawLevels, expected)
    if (length(unmatched)) add_issue(sprintf(
      "suspicion_map: raw labels not in config: %s | expected one of: %s",
      paste(shQuote(unmatched), collapse = ", "),
      paste(shQuote(expected),  collapse = ", ")))
    if (sum(!is.na(data$suspicion)) == 0)
      add_issue("suspicion_map produced 0 non-NA values — every row failed lookup. Check cfg$suspicion_map against your oTree choice labels.")
  } else add_warn("suspicionRaw absent or all-NA — primary models will run without a covariate.")

  # 2. Manipulation-recall coding
  if ("manipLabelText" %in% names(data) && sum(!is.na(data$manipLabelText)) > 5 &&
      sum(!is.na(data$manipLabelAccurate)) == 0)
    add_issue("manipLabelAccurate is all-NA despite manipLabelText having values. cfg$manip_label_pattern_* don't match your oTree text.")
  if ("manipTransText" %in% names(data) && sum(!is.na(data$manipTransText)) > 5 &&
      sum(!is.na(data$manipTransAccurate)) == 0)
    add_issue("manipTransAccurate is all-NA despite manipTransText having values. cfg$manip_trans_pattern_* don't match your oTree text.")

  # 3. Factor levels
  if (!setequal(levels(data$Label), cfg$label_levels))
    add_issue(sprintf("Label levels mismatch. Got: %s | Expected: %s",
              paste(shQuote(levels(data$Label)), collapse = ", "),
              paste(shQuote(cfg$label_levels),    collapse = ", ")))
  if (!setequal(levels(data$Transparency), cfg$transparency_levels))
    add_issue(sprintf("Transparency levels mismatch. Got: %s | Expected: %s",
              paste(shQuote(levels(data$Transparency)),    collapse = ", "),
              paste(shQuote(cfg$transparency_levels),      collapse = ", ")))

  # 4. Composite scores
  if (sum(!is.na(data$trustMayer))    == 0) add_issue("trustMayer is all-NA. Check Mayer item names in renameMap.")
  if (sum(!is.na(data$openingDemand)) == 0) add_issue("openingDemand is all-NA. Check demandR1 in renameMap.")

  # 5. Demand columns for cfg$n_rounds
  expectedRounds <- paste0("demandR", seq_len(cfg$n_rounds))
  presentRounds  <- vapply(expectedRounds,
                           \(v) v %in% names(data) && sum(!is.na(data[[v]])) > 0,
                           logical(1))
  if (any(!presentRounds))
    add_warn(sprintf("Demand columns missing or all-NA: %s",
                     paste(expectedRounds[!presentRounds], collapse = ", ")))

  # 6. Covariate availability
  for (cv in cfg$covariates) {
    if (!cv %in% names(data) ||
        sum(!is.na(data[[cv]])) < cfg$covariate_min_nonNA ||
        length(unique(na.omit(data[[cv]]))) < cfg$covariate_min_distinct) {
      add_warn(sprintf("Covariate '%s' not usable in this export — primary models will run without it.", cv))
    }
  }


 # 7. Gender label
  if ("gender" %in% names(data) && sum(!is.na(data$gender)) > 5) {
    seenGenders     <- unique(na.omit(data$gender[data$gender != ""]))
    expectedGenders <- cfg$gender_categories
    missing <- setdiff(expectedGenders, seenGenders)
    extra   <- setdiff(seenGenders, expectedGenders)
    if (length(seenGenders) == 1)
      add_warn(sprintf("Gender column has only one value: %s — limited demographic variety.",
                       paste(shQuote(seenGenders), collapse = ", ")))
    if (length(missing) > 0 && length(seenGenders) > 1)
      add_warn(sprintf("Expected gender categories absent from data: %s",
                       paste(shQuote(missing), collapse = ", ")))
    if (length(extra) > 0)
      add_warn(sprintf("Unexpected gender values in data (not in cfg$gender_categories): %s",
                       paste(shQuote(extra), collapse = ", ")))
  }

  # 8. Chat sender label
  if ("chatLog" %in% names(data) && sum(!is.na(data$chatLog) & data$chatLog != "") > 5) {
    sample_chat <- na.omit(data$chatLog)[1]
    parsed <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(sample_chat), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(parsed) && "sender" %in% names(parsed)) {
      seenSenders <- unique(parsed$sender)
      if (!cfg$chat_sender_participant %in% seenSenders)
        add_warn(sprintf("cfg$chat_sender_participant = '%s' not in chatLog senders. Senders seen in first row: %s",
                cfg$chat_sender_participant,
                paste(shQuote(seenSenders), collapse = ", ")))
    }
  }

  # Print
  cat("\nDATA HEALTH CHECK\n")
  if (length(issues)) {
    cat("FATAL ISSUES (downstream chunks will produce wrong results):\n")
    for (m in issues) cat("  ✗ ", m, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (length(warns)) {
    cat("WARNINGS (degraded analysis, not fatal):\n")
    for (m in warns)  cat("  ⚠ ", m, "\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!length(issues) && !length(warns))
    cat("✓ All checks passed.\n")
  invisible(list(issues = issues, warns = warns))
}
```

# 1. Data — load oTree wide export

```{r data-path}
dataPath <- analysis_config$data_path
stopifnot(file.exists(dataPath))
raw <- read.csv(dataPath, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cat("Loaded:", nrow(raw), "rows ×", ncol(raw), "columns\n")

# CONSORT-style flow
consort <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    consented      = !is.na(introduction.1.player.consent) & introduction.1.player.consent == 1,
    declined       = !is.na(introduction.1.player.declined) & introduction.1.player.declined == 1,
    reachedOutcome = !is.na(participant.final_share),
    completedTrust = !is.na(post_survey.1.player.comp_1)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    allocated      = n(),
    consented      = sum(consented, na.rm = TRUE),
    declined       = sum(declined, na.rm = TRUE),
    reachedOutcome = sum(reachedOutcome, na.rm = TRUE),
    completedTrust = sum(completedTrust, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
cat("\nParticipant flow\n")
cat(sprintf("  Export rows:                %d\n", consort$allocated))
cat(sprintf("  Consented:                  %d  (declined %d; the rest are unfilled buffer slots)\n",
            consort$consented, consort$declined))
cat(sprintf("  Reached an outcome:         %d  (%d consented withdrew before an outcome)\n",
            consort$reachedOutcome, consort$consented - consort$reachedOutcome))
cat(sprintf("  Completed the trust survey: %d\n", consort$completedTrust))
cat(sprintf("  Analytical sample (positive share): applied next chunk, N = 201\n"))
```

```{r data-rename}
absent  <- setdiff(renameMap, names(raw))

  message("Skipping ", length(absent), " column(s) not found in this export:\n  ",
          paste(absent, collapse = "\n  "))

data <- raw %>% rename(!!!present)

# Type-aware placeholders: text columns get NA_character_, numerics NA_real_,
# so downstream str_detect and case_when calls behave correctly.
```

## 1b. Recode & compute composites

```{r data-recode}
# Coerce oTree string-encoded numerics
roundCols <- c(paste0("demandR",     seq_len(cfg$n_rounds)),
               paste0("botCounterR", seq_len(cfg$n_rounds)))

numericCols <- c(
  "agreed","agreementRound","finalShare","totalBonus",
  "preFairSplit","preFairConf","preTrustComp","preTrustFair","preTrustOverall",
  "comp1","comp2","comp3","ben1","ben2","ben3","pred1","pred2","overallTrust",
  "godNatural","godHumanlike","godLifelike","godHumanlikeness",
  "postFairSplit","perceivedExploit","age",
  "trustProp1","trustProp2","trustProp3","trustPropensity",
  "chatFairSplit","finalTrustChat",
  "negExperience","aiFamiliarity",
  "otreePercComp","otreePercPred","otreePercBen","otreeTrustComp",
  paste0("botAcceptedR",     seq_len(cfg$n_rounds)),
  paste0("acceptedCounterR", seq_len(cfg$n_rounds)),
  roundCols
)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(across(any_of(numericCols), \(x) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))))

# Mean-of-available-items composite (returns NA when whole scale is empty)
rowMeanK <- function(...) {
  vals <- c(...)
  if (all(is.na(vals))) NA_real_ else mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Helper: collect demand columns based on cfg$n_rounds
demandColNames <- paste0("demandR", seq_len(cfg$n_rounds))

data <- data %>%
  mutate(across(any_of(c("manipLabelText","manipTransText","suspicionRaw",
                         "suspicionReason","chatLog","strategy",
                         "Label","Transparency","gender","dataConsent")),
                as.character)) %>%
  mutate(gender = ifelse(gender == "", NA_character_, gender)) %>%
  mutate(
    Label = factor(str_to_title(Label),
                   levels = c("Human", "Ai"),
                   labels = cfg$label_levels),
    Transparency = factor(str_to_title(Transparency),
                          levels = cfg$transparency_levels),

    suspicion = as.numeric(cfg$suspicion_map[suspicionRaw]),

    manipLabelAccurate = case_when(
      Label == cfg$label_levels[1] &
        str_detect(manipLabelText, fixed(cfg$manip_label_pattern_human,
                                         ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ 1L,
      Label == cfg$label_levels[2] &
        str_detect(manipLabelText, fixed(cfg$manip_label_pattern_ai,
                                         ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ 1L,
      str_detect(manipLabelText, fixed(cfg$manip_dont_remember,
                                       ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ NA_integer_,
      TRUE ~ 0L),
    manipTransAccurate = case_when(
      Transparency == cfg$transparency_levels[2] &
        str_detect(manipTransText, fixed(cfg$manip_trans_pattern_yes,
                                         ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ 1L,
      Transparency == cfg$transparency_levels[1] &
        str_detect(manipTransText, fixed(cfg$manip_trans_pattern_no,
                                         ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ 1L,
      str_detect(manipTransText, fixed(cfg$manip_dont_remember,
                                       ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ NA_integer_,
      TRUE ~ 0L),

    competence     = pmap_dbl(across(c(comp1, comp2, comp3)), rowMeanK),
    benevolence    = pmap_dbl(across(c(ben1,  ben2,  ben3)),  rowMeanK),
    predictability = pmap_dbl(across(c(pred1, pred2)),         rowMeanK),
    trustMayer     = pmap_dbl(across(c(competence, benevolence, predictability)), rowMeanK),
    anthropomorphism = pmap_dbl(across(c(godNatural, godHumanlike, godLifelike)), rowMeanK),

    openingDemand = .data[[demandColNames[1]]],
    finalDemand   = pmap_dbl(across(all_of(demandColNames)), \(...) {
      v <- c(...); v <- v[!is.na(v)]
      if (length(v) == 0) NA_real_ else tail(v, 1)
    }),
    concession    = openingDemand - finalDemand,
    demandSlope   = pmap_dbl(across(all_of(demandColNames)), \(...) {
      v <- c(...); v <- v[!is.na(v)]
      if (length(v) < 2) 0 else coef(lm(v ~ seq_along(v)))[2]
    }),

    # Numeric contrasts for SEM (Label: AI=1, Human=0)
    labelContrast = as.numeric(Label == cfg$label_levels[2]),
    transContrast = as.numeric(Transparency == cfg$transparency_levels[2])
  )

if (!"offScriptPct" %in% names(data)) data$offScriptPct <- NA_real_

cat("Cell counts:\n"); print(with(data, table(Label, Transparency)))

cat(sprintf("\nAnalytical sample:             %d\n", nrow(data)))
cat(sprintf("  behavioural outcomes:        %d\n", nrow(data)))
cat(sprintf("  trust models (+ suspicion):    %d\n",
            sum(!is.na(data$trustMayer) & !is.na(data$suspicion))))
cat(sprintf("  demographic moderation:        %d\n",
            sum(!is.na(data$trustMayer) & !is.na(data$suspicion) & !is.na(data$age))))

## API stall rate (diagnostic covariate not pre-registered)
# Fallback stall messages appear when the OpenAI API fails.
# Higher stall rates reduce conversational fluency and may increase AI suspicion.
STALL_PHRASES <- c("one sec", "hmm give me a sec", "hang on", "hold on a min",
                    "one min", "just a sec", "bear with me", "sec")

computeStallRate <- function(chatJSON) {
  if (is.na(chatJSON) || chatJSON == "") return(NA_real_)
  msgs <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(chatJSON), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(msgs) || !is.data.frame(msgs)) return(NA_real_)
  botMsgs <- msgs$text[msgs$sender == "partner"]
  if (length(botMsgs) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  nStalls <- sum(tolower(trimws(botMsgs)) %in% STALL_PHRASES)
  nStalls / length(botMsgs)
}

data$stallRate <- vapply(data$chatLog, computeStallRate, numeric(1))
cat(sprintf("\nStall rate: M = %.3f, SD = %.3f, range = [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            mean(data$stallRate, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd(data$stallRate, na.rm = TRUE),
            min(data$stallRate, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(data$stallRate, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Correlation with suspicion: r = %.3f\n",
            cor(data$stallRate, data$suspicion, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")))
```
## 1c. Surface-register audit of counterpart text

Fidelity check on the two register features the enforcement pipeline did not control: message length and lexical diversity. Em-dash rate confirms the Step-1 strip ran. Surface only: does not certify perceptual match.

```{r surface-audit}
auditPartnerText <- function(chatJSON) {
  out <- c(wordsPerMsg = NA_real_, ttr = NA_real_, emDashPer100 = NA_real_)
  if (is.na(chatJSON) || chatJSON == "") return(out)
  msgs <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(chatJSON), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(msgs) || !is.data.frame(msgs)) return(out)
  txt <- msgs$text[msgs$sender == "partner"]
  txt <- txt[!is.na(txt) & !(tolower(trimws(txt)) %in% STALL_PHRASES)]
  if (length(txt) == 0) return(out)
  joined <- tolower(paste(txt, collapse = " "))
  words  <- unlist(strsplit(joined, "\\s+")); words <- words[words != ""]
  nW <- length(words)
  if (nW == 0) return(out)
  out["wordsPerMsg"]  <- nW / length(txt)
  out["ttr"]          <- length(unique(words)) / nW
  out["emDashPer100"] <- 100 * lengths(regmatches(joined,
                            gregexpr("\u2014|--", joined))) / nW
  out
}

audit <- t(vapply(data$chatLog, auditPartnerText, numeric(3)))
data  <- cbind(data, as.data.frame(audit))

cat(sprintf("Partner text audit computed for %d participants (%d with usable text)\n",
            nrow(data), sum(!is.na(data$wordsPerMsg))))
cat(sprintf("Em-dash rate per 100 words: M = %.4f (strip check, expect ~0)\n",
            mean(data$emDashPer100, na.rm = TRUE)))
```
## 1d. Extended surface-register features

Five further features on the counterpart's uncontrolled writing, of the same surface family as §1c: function-word ratio, mean word length, message-length variability, hapax ratio, and punctuation rate. Like §1c, these test condition differences, not the offScriptPct covariate.

```{r surface-audit-extended}
# O'Shea, Bandar & Crockett (2012) 277-word function-word list, read from file.
FN_WORDS <- read.csv("oshea_function_words_277.csv",
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$function_word

extendedTextFeatures <- function(chatJSON) {
  out <- c(fnWordRatio = NA_real_, meanWordLen = NA_real_,
           sentLenSD = NA_real_, hapaxRatio = NA_real_,
           punctPer100 = NA_real_)
  if (is.na(chatJSON) || chatJSON == "") return(out)
  msgs <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON(chatJSON), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(msgs) || !is.data.frame(msgs)) return(out)
  txt <- msgs$text[msgs$sender == "partner"]
  txt <- txt[!is.na(txt) & !(tolower(trimws(txt)) %in% STALL_PHRASES)]
  if (length(txt) == 0) return(out)

  joined <- tolower(paste(txt, collapse = " "))
  words  <- unlist(strsplit(joined, "\\s+")); words <- words[words != ""]
  nW <- length(words); if (nW == 0) return(out)

  out["fnWordRatio"] <- sum(words %in% FN_WORDS) / nW
  out["meanWordLen"] <- mean(nchar(words))
  wc <- vapply(txt, function(s) length(strsplit(trimws(s), "\\s+")[[1]]),
               numeric(1))
  out["sentLenSD"]   <- if (length(wc) > 1) sd(wc) else 0
  tb <- table(words)
  out["hapaxRatio"]  <- sum(tb == 1) / nW
  out["punctPer100"] <- 100 * sum(gregexpr("[[:punct:]]", joined)[[1]] > 0) / nW
  out
}

extAudit <- t(vapply(data$chatLog, extendedTextFeatures, numeric(5)))
data[, colnames(extAudit)] <- as.data.frame(extAudit)
cat(sprintf("Extended features for %d participants; function-word list = %d words.\n",
            nrow(data), length(FN_WORDS)))
```

## 1g. Convergent-validity cross-check vs oTree's server-computed composites

oTree's `post_survey` app stores its own item-level aggregates (`perc_competence`, `perc_predictability`, `perc_benevolence`, `trust_composite`). Our §1b composites should match these to rounding error. A correlation noticeably below 1.0 indicates an item-aggregation bug (wrong items, wrong rownames, or NA-handling divergence). This is a one-off check, not a reportable analysis.

```{r composite-cross-check}
crossCheck <- tibble(
  Pair = c("Competence",
           "Predictability",
           "Benevolence",
           "Mayer total"),
  ours    = c("competence", "predictability", "benevolence", "trustMayer"),
  otree   = c("otreePercComp", "otreePercPred", "otreePercBen", "otreeTrustComp")
) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    n_compared = sum(complete.cases(data[[ours]], data[[otree]])),
    r          = if (n_compared > 2)
                   cor(data[[ours]], data[[otree]], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
                 else NA_real_,
    # Rescale our 1–5 composite to 0–1 to match oTree's normalised scale
    # before computing residual difference. r = 1 with max_diff ≈ 0 confirms
    # the composites match exactly modulo scale.
    max_abs_diff = if (n_compared > 0)
                     max(abs((data[[ours]] - 1) / 4 - data[[otree]]), na.rm = TRUE)
                   else NA_real_
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Pair, n_compared, r, max_abs_diff)

knitr::kable(roundDF(crossCheck, 4),
             caption = "Cross-check: our §1b composites (rescaled to 0–1) vs oTree's stored composites (r should be ≈ 1.00, max_abs_diff ≈ 0)")

if (any(crossCheck$r < 0.99 & !is.na(crossCheck$r)))
  warning("Composite cross-check: at least one r < .99. Investigate item aggregation.")
```

# 3. Reliability & measurement validation

## 3a. Cronbach's α

```{r reliability}
safeAlpha <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>% mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
               select(where(\(x) sum(!is.na(x)) >= 2 && var(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 0))
  if (ncol(df) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  suppressWarnings(psych::alpha(df, warnings = FALSE))$total$raw_alpha
}

reliability <- tibble(
  Scale = c("Competence (Mayer)", "Benevolence (Mayer)", "Predictability (Mayer)",
            "Mayer total (8 items)", "Anthropomorphism (Godspeed)",
            "Trust propensity (3 items)"),
  kItems = c(3, 3, 2, 8, 3, 3),
  alpha = round(c(
    safeAlpha(data %>% select(comp1, comp2, comp3)),
    safeAlpha(data %>% select(ben1, ben2, ben3)),
    safeAlpha(data %>% select(pred1, pred2)),
    safeAlpha(data %>% select(comp1, comp2, comp3,
                              pred1, pred2,
                              ben1, ben2, ben3)),
    safeAlpha(data %>% select(godNatural, godHumanlike, godLifelike)),
    safeAlpha(data %>% select(trustProp1, trustProp2, trustProp3))
  ), 3)
)
knitr::kable(reliability, caption = "Table 3. Internal consistency")
```

## 3b. CFA on the Mayer 8-item three-factor structure

CFA validates the measurement structure used as composite scores downstream — we do **not** propagate the latent variable into the structural model. Discriminant validity is judged with the Fornell–Larcker criterion (√AVE > inter-factor *r*).

```{r cfa}
cfaItems <- data %>% select(comp1, comp2, comp3,
                            ben1, ben2, ben3,
                            pred1, pred2)

itemDiag <- tibble(
  item     = names(cfaItems),
  n_valid  = sapply(cfaItems, \(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
  variance = sapply(cfaItems, \(x) if (sum(!is.na(x)) > 1) var(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_)
)
goodItems <- itemDiag$item[itemDiag$n_valid >= 10 &
                           !is.na(itemDiag$variance) & itemDiag$variance > 0]

factorMap <- list(
  competence     = intersect(c("comp1","comp2","comp3"), goodItems),
  benevolence    = intersect(c("ben1","ben2","ben3"),    goodItems),
  predictability = intersect(c("pred1","pred2"),         goodItems)
) |> (\(L) L[lengths(L) >= 2])()

cfaFit <- NULL
if (length(factorMap) >= 2) {
  cfaModel <- paste(
    sapply(names(factorMap), \(f) {
      its <- factorMap[[f]]
      # When two-indicator factors are under-identified, they can throw Heywood cases
      # (standardised loading > 1, negative residual variance). Constrain the
      # two loadings to equality to identify the factor — standard practice.
      if (length(its) == 2)
        paste0(f, " =~ v*", its[1], " + v*", its[2])
      else
        paste0(f, " =~ ", paste(its, collapse = " + "))
    }),
    collapse = "\n")
  cfaFit <- cfa(cfaModel,
                data = cfaItems[, unlist(factorMap), drop = FALSE],
                estimator = "ML", missing = "fiml")
}

if (!is.null(cfaFit)) {
  fmCFA <- fitMeasures(cfaFit, c("chisq","df","pvalue","cfi","tli","rmsea","srmr"))
  cat(sprintf("CFA: χ²(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %s | CFI = %.3f, TLI = %.3f, RMSEA = %.3f, SRMR = %.3f\n",
              fmCFA["df"], fmCFA["chisq"], formatP(fmCFA["pvalue"]),
              fmCFA["cfi"], fmCFA["tli"], fmCFA["rmsea"], fmCFA["srmr"]))

  loads <- standardizedSolution(cfaFit) %>%
    filter(op == "=~") %>% select(lhs, rhs, est.std, se, pvalue) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))
  print(knitr::kable(loads, caption = "Table 4. Standardised factor loadings"))

  factors <- unique(loads$lhs); CR <- AVE <- numeric(length(factors))
  names(CR) <- names(AVE) <- factors
  for (f in factors) {
    l <- loads$est.std[loads$lhs == f]
    CR[f]  <- sum(l)^2 / (sum(l)^2 + sum(1 - l^2))
    AVE[f] <- sum(l^2)  / (sum(l^2)  + sum(1 - l^2))
  }
  print(knitr::kable(
    tibble(Factor = factors, CR = round(CR, 3),
           AVE = round(AVE, 3), sqrtAVE = round(sqrt(AVE), 3)),
    caption = "Table 5. Composite reliability and AVE"))

  if (length(factors) >= 2) {
    facCors <- lavInspect(cfaFit, "cor.lv")
    cat("\nFactor correlations:\n"); print(round(facCors, 3))
    cat("\nFornell–Larcker discriminant validity (√AVE > max |r|):\n")
    for (f in factors) {
      others <- abs(facCors[f, setdiff(factors, f)])
      cat("  ", f, ": √AVE =", round(sqrt(AVE[f]), 3),
          "vs max r =", round(max(others), 3),
          if (sqrt(AVE[f]) > max(others)) "✓" else "✗", "\n")
    }
  }
} else {
  cat("CFA skipped — fewer than 2 factors with ≥2 usable indicators.\n")
}
```

## 3c. CFA path diagram (publication figure)

Visual rendering of the three-factor measurement model. Latent factors at top (ovals), observed indicators at bottom (rectangles), arrows labelled with standardised loadings, curved arrows showing inter-factor correlations, fit indices in a footer band. 

```{r cfa-diagram, fig.height = 7}
if (!is.null(cfaFit)) {
  loads <- standardizedSolution(cfaFit) %>%
    filter(op == "=~") %>%
    select(factor = lhs, item = rhs, loading = est.std, p = pvalue)

  resVars <- standardizedSolution(cfaFit) %>%
    filter(op == "~~", lhs == rhs, lhs %in% loads$item) %>%
    select(item = lhs, resid = est.std)

  facCors <- lavInspect(cfaFit, "cor.lv")
  fitInd  <- fitMeasures(cfaFit, c("chisq","df","pvalue","cfi","tli","rmsea","srmr"))

  factorOrder  <- intersect(c("competence","benevolence","predictability"),
                            unique(loads$factor))
  factorLabels <- c(competence = "Competence",
                    benevolence = "Benevolence",
                    predictability = "Predictability")
  itemLabels <- c(comp1 = "comp_1", comp2 = "comp_2", comp3 = "comp_3",
                  ben1 = "ben_1",   ben2 = "ben_2",   ben3 = "ben_3",
                  pred1 = "pred_1", pred2 = "pred_2")

  nFac   <- length(factorOrder)
  facX   <- setNames(seq(2.5, 9.5, length.out = nFac), factorOrder)
  facY   <- 5.0

  facCol      <- setNames(rep("#1A5276", nFac), factorOrder)
  facColLight <- setNames(rep("#AED6F1", nFac), factorOrder)

  itemPositions <- loads %>%
    group_by(factor) %>%
    mutate(within = row_number(),
           total  = n(),
           xCenter = facX[as.character(factor)],
           xOffset = (within - (total + 1) / 2) * 0.95,
           x = xCenter + xOffset,
           y = 1.4) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(labelX = (xCenter + x) / 2,
           labelY = (facY - 0.45 + y + 0.32) / 2) %>%
    left_join(resVars, by = "item")

  arcLayers <- list()
  if (nFac >= 2) {
    pairs <- combn(factorOrder, 2, simplify = FALSE)
    for (pr in pairs) {
      x1 <- facX[pr[1]]; x2 <- facX[pr[2]]
      isAdjacent <- abs(which(factorOrder == pr[1]) -
                        which(factorOrder == pr[2])) == 1
      r <- facCors[pr[1], pr[2]]
      arcStartY <- facY + 0.45
      midX <- (x1 + x2) / 2
      apexY <- if (isAdjacent) facY + 0.95 else facY + 1.65
      curveAmt <- if (isAdjacent) -0.45 else -0.55
      arcLayers <- c(arcLayers, list(
        annotate("curve",
                 x = x1 + 0.55, xend = midX - 0.25,
                 y = arcStartY, yend = apexY,
                 curvature = curveAmt * 0.6,
                 linewidth = 0.5, colour = subtleCol, linetype = "dashed"),
        annotate("curve",
                 x = midX + 0.25, xend = x2 - 0.55,
                 y = apexY, yend = arcStartY,
                 curvature = curveAmt * 0.6,
                 linewidth = 0.5, colour = subtleCol, linetype = "dashed"),
        annotate("text", x = midX, y = apexY + 0.08,
                 label = sprintf("%.2f", r),
                 size = 3.3, fontface = "italic", colour = pathCol)
      ))
    }
  }

  ovalAngles <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = 100)
  latentLayers <- list()
  for (f in factorOrder) {
    latentLayers <- c(latentLayers, list(
      annotate("polygon",
               x = facX[f] + 1.05 * cos(ovalAngles),
               y = facY    + 0.50 * sin(ovalAngles),
               fill = facColLight[f], alpha = 0.45, colour = NA),
      annotate("path",
               x = facX[f] + 1.05 * cos(ovalAngles),
               y = facY    + 0.50 * sin(ovalAngles),
               colour = facCol[f], linewidth = 1.3),
      annotate("text", x = facX[f], y = facY,
               label = factorLabels[f],
               size = 5.0, fontface = "bold", colour = facCol[f])
    ))
  }

  qcCol <- function(value, type) {
    if (is.na(value)) return(subtleCol)
    if (type %in% c("cfi","tli")) {
      if (value >= 0.95) sigCol else if (value >= 0.90) hlCol else nullCol
    } else if (type == "rmsea") {
      if (value <= 0.06) sigCol else if (value <= 0.08) hlCol else nullCol
    } else if (type == "srmr") {
      if (value <= 0.05) sigCol else if (value <= 0.08) hlCol else nullCol
    } else mainCol
  }

  residualLayers <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(itemPositions))) {
    ix      <- itemPositions$x[i]
    boxBot  <- itemPositions$y[i] - 0.28
    rv      <- itemPositions$resid[i]
    circR   <- 0.24
    circY   <- boxBot - 0.62
    circAng <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 60)
    selfAng <- seq(pi * 1.25, pi * 1.75, length.out = 30)
    selfX   <- ix + (circR + 0.14) * cos(selfAng)
    selfY   <- circY + (circR + 0.14) * sin(selfAng)
    residualLayers <- c(residualLayers, list(
      annotate("segment",
               x = ix, xend = ix,
               y = circY + circR, yend = boxBot,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.14, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               colour = subtleCol, linewidth = 0.4),
      annotate("path",
               x = ix + circR * cos(circAng),
               y = circY + circR * sin(circAng),
               colour = subtleCol, linewidth = 0.45),
      annotate("text", x = ix, y = circY,
               label = paste0("e", i),
               size = 2.7, colour = subtleCol, fontface = "italic"),
      annotate("curve",
               x = selfX[1], xend = selfX[length(selfX)],
               y = selfY[1], yend = selfY[length(selfY)],
               curvature = 0.9,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.08, "cm"), ends = "both", type = "closed"),
               colour = subtleCol, linewidth = 0.35),
      annotate("text", x = ix, y = circY - circR - 0.52,
               label = if (is.na(rv)) "" else sprintf("%.2f", rv),
               size = 2.5, colour = subtleCol)
    ))
  }

  p <- ggplot() +
    arcLayers +
    latentLayers +

    {
      ap <- itemPositions %>%
        mutate(x0 = xCenter, y0 = facY - 0.45,
               x1 = x,        y1 = y + 0.32,
               gapFrac = 0.16,
               gxA = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (0.5 - gapFrac),
               gyA = y0 + (y1 - y0) * (0.5 - gapFrac),
               gxB = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (0.5 + gapFrac),
               gyB = y0 + (y1 - y0) * (0.5 + gapFrac),
               midGapX = (x0 + x1) / 2,
               midGapY = (y0 + y1) / 2)
      list(
        geom_segment(data = ap,
          aes(x = x0, xend = gxA, y = y0, yend = gyA, colour = factor),
          linewidth = ap$loading * 1.6, show.legend = FALSE),
        geom_segment(data = ap,
          aes(x = gxB, xend = x1, y = gyB, yend = y1, colour = factor),
          linewidth = ap$loading * 1.6,
          arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed"),
          show.legend = FALSE),
        geom_text(data = ap,
          aes(x = midGapX, y = midGapY, label = sprintf("%.2f", loading),
              colour = factor),
          size = 3.4, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE)
      )
    } +

    geom_rect(data = itemPositions,
              aes(xmin = x - 0.38, xmax = x + 0.38,
                  ymin = y - 0.28, ymax = y + 0.28,
                  fill = factor),
              alpha = 0.20, colour = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_rect(data = itemPositions,
              aes(xmin = x - 0.38, xmax = x + 0.38,
                  ymin = y - 0.28, ymax = y + 0.28,
                  colour = factor),
              fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = itemPositions,
              aes(x = x, y = y, label = itemLabels[as.character(item)]),
              size = 3.3, colour = mainCol) +

    residualLayers +

    annotate("segment", x = 0.3, xend = 11.7, y = -0.6, yend = -0.6,
             colour = "#E5E7E9", linewidth = 0.4) +
    annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = -0.95,
             label = sprintf("CFI = %.3f", fitInd["cfi"]),
             size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
             colour = qcCol(fitInd["cfi"], "cfi")) +
    annotate("text", x = 3.5, y = -0.95,
             label = sprintf("TLI = %.3f", fitInd["tli"]),
             size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
             colour = qcCol(fitInd["tli"], "tli")) +
    annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = -0.95,
             label = sprintf("RMSEA = %.3f", fitInd["rmsea"]),
             size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
             colour = qcCol(fitInd["rmsea"], "rmsea")) +
    annotate("text", x = 7.5, y = -0.95,
             label = sprintf("SRMR = %.3f", fitInd["srmr"]),
             size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
             colour = qcCol(fitInd["srmr"], "srmr")) +
    annotate("text", x = 10, y = -0.95,
             label = sprintf("chi-sq(%.0f) = %.2f",
                             fitInd["df"], fitInd["chisq"]),
             size = 3.5, colour = mainCol) +
    annotate("point", x = 3.5, y = -1.4, size = 2.5, colour = sigCol) +
    annotate("text", x = 3.8, y = -1.4, label = "good",
             size = 3, colour = sigCol, hjust = 0) +
    annotate("point", x = 5.2, y = -1.4, size = 2.5, colour = hlCol) +
    annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = -1.4, label = "acceptable",
             size = 3, colour = hlCol, hjust = 0) +
    annotate("point", x = 7.2, y = -1.4, size = 2.5, colour = nullCol) +
    annotate("text", x = 7.5, y = -1.4, label = "poor",
             size = 3, colour = nullCol, hjust = 0) +

    scale_colour_manual(values = facCol) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = facCol) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.3, 11.7), ylim = c(-2.3, 7.2), clip = "off") +
    labs(title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(20, 15, 15, 15))

  print(p)

  figText(
    "Confirmatory factor analysis of the eight-item Mayer trust scale",
    "Standardised three-factor solution (competence, benevolence, predictability)")
} else {
  cat("CFA diagram skipped — fitted model is unavailable.\n")
}
```

# 4. Manipulation & realism checks

## 4a. Anthropomorphism (Godspeed) by Label and Transparency

Pre-registered prediction: AI < Human on humanlikeness. The 2×2 ANOVA also lets us check whether Transparency moves the realism perception (it shouldn't — the chat-medium affordances are crossed with Label, not Transparency).

```{r mc-anthro}
modAnthro <- aov(addCovariates(anthropomorphism ~ Label * Transparency, data),
                 data = data)
print(tidyAnova3(modAnthro))

cat("\nMean anthropomorphism by Label:\n")
print(data %>% group_by(Label) %>%
        summarise(M = mean(anthropomorphism, na.rm = TRUE),
                  SD = sd(anthropomorphism, na.rm = TRUE), n = n()))
gAnthro <- effectsize::hedges_g(anthropomorphism ~ Label, data = data)
cat(sprintf("\nLabel contrast: g = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]\n",
            gAnthro$Hedges_g, gAnthro$CI_low, gAnthro$CI_high))
```

## 4b. Recall accuracy on the manipulations

```{r mc-recall}
# Guard: if a manipulation-recall column is missing, yield an empty table rather than error.
if (!"manipLabelAccurate" %in% names(data)) data$manipLabelAccurate <- NA_integer_
if (!"manipTransAccurate" %in% names(data)) data$manipTransAccurate <- NA_integer_

recallTab <- data %>%
  pivot_longer(c(manipLabelAccurate, manipTransAccurate),
               names_to = "Check", values_to = "Accurate") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Accurate)) %>%
  group_by(Check) %>%
  summarise(n           = n(),
            nAccurate   = sum(Accurate),
            pctAccurate = mean(Accurate) * 100,
            binomP      = formatP(binom.test(sum(Accurate), n(), 0.5)$p.value),
            .groups     = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Check = dplyr::case_when(Check == "manipLabelAccurate" ~ "Label recall",
                                  Check == "manipTransAccurate" ~ "Transparency recall"))
knitr::kable(roundDF(recallTab),
             caption = "Table 6. Manipulation recall — proportion accurate (vs chance .50)")
```

## 4c. Manipulation check — detection of partner identity

Suspicion is a continuous covariate in all primary models (§9), used for exclusion only in a sensitivity analysis (§20), never to drop participants from the primary tests.

```{r mc-suspicion, fig.height = 5}
if (!requireNamespace("ggbeeswarm", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("ggbeeswarm", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(ggbeeswarm)

suspData <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(suspicion)) %>%
  mutate(
    correct = (Label == "Human" & suspicion <= 3) | (Label == "AI" & suspicion >= 4),
    suspLabel = factor(suspicion,
      levels = 1:6,
      labels = c("Definitely\nhuman","Very likely\nhuman","Probably\nhuman",
                 "Probably\nAI","Very likely\nAI","Definitely\nAI"))
  )

suspMeans <- suspData %>%
  group_by(Label) %>%
  summarise(M = mean(suspicion), .groups = "drop")

suspAcc <- suspData %>%
  group_by(Label) %>%
  summarise(acc = mean(correct) * 100, .groups = "drop")

# Two-band detection: leaned human (<=3) vs leaned AI (>=4)
waffleDF <- suspData %>%
  mutate(belief = factor(ifelse(suspicion >= 4, "Leaned AI", "Leaned human"),
                         levels = c("Leaned human", "Leaned AI"))) %>%
  arrange(Label, belief) %>%
  group_by(Label) %>%
  mutate(idx = row_number() - 1,
         col = idx %% 10,
         row = idx %/% 10) %>%
  ungroup()

waffleMeans <- suspData %>%
  group_by(Label) %>%
  summarise(M = mean(suspicion),
            pctAI = mean(suspicion >= 4) * 100, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(waffleDF, aes(col, row, fill = belief)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.1, width = 0.92, height = 0.92) +
  facet_wrap(~ Label, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Leaned human" = accentCol, "Leaned AI" = hlCol),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", colour = mainCol),
        panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(20, 15, 15, 15))

figText(
  "Detection of partner identity by condition",
  "Each square is one participant; colour = which way they leaned")
```

## 4d. Pre-negotiation expectations by Label (baseline check)
```{r}
# The label is revealed at partner confirmation, BEFORE the negotiation.
# If it shapes trust through a prior, pre-negotiation expectations should already
# differ by condition. This checks whether the label moved any baseline measure —
# before the counterpart had done anything.

preMeasures <- c(
  preTrustOverall = "Pre-trust: overall",
  preTrustComp    = "Pre-trust: competence",
  preTrustFair    = "Pre-trust: fairness",
  preFairSplit    = "Pre: expected fair split (%)",
  preFairConf     = "Pre: fairness confidence"
)

preTab <- imap_dfr(preMeasures, function(label, var) {
  if (!var %in% names(data)) return(NULL)
  dd <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var]]))
  ai <- dd %>% filter(Label == "AI")    %>% pull(.data[[var]])
  hu <- dd %>% filter(Label == "Human") %>% pull(.data[[var]])
  if (length(ai) < 2 || length(hu) < 2) return(NULL)
  tt <- t.test(ai, hu)
  g  <- effectsize::hedges_g(ai, hu)
  tibble(
    Measure = label,
    AI    = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(ai), sd(ai)),
    Human = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(hu), sd(hu)),
    t     = round(unname(tt$statistic), 2),
    df    = round(unname(tt$parameter), 1),
    p     = formatP(tt$p.value),
    g     = round(g$Hedges_g, 2)
  )
})

knitr::kable(preTab,
  caption = "Table 7. Pre-negotiation expectations by Label. AI and Human columns show M (SD); Welch's t.")
```
## 4e. Counterpart text: surface-register audit by Label

The enforcement pipeline (Appendix J.6) held register constant by regenerating on a 396-term lexicon, so tell-counts cannot serve as a fidelity check: the filter removed them by construction. What it did not govern is message length and lexical diversity. A Label difference on those features would show the counterpart's uncontrolled writing varied by condition; a null supports register-constancy. This is a surface check and does not certify perceptual match.

```{r}
auditMeasures <- c(
  wordsPerMsg = "Words per partner message",
  ttr         = "Type-token ratio (lexical diversity)"
)
auditTab <- imap_dfr(auditMeasures, function(label, var) {
  if (!var %in% names(data)) return(NULL)
  dd <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var]]))
  ai <- dd %>% filter(Label == "AI")    %>% pull(.data[[var]])
  hu <- dd %>% filter(Label == "Human") %>% pull(.data[[var]])
  if (length(ai) < 2 || length(hu) < 2) return(NULL)
  tt <- t.test(ai, hu)
  g  <- effectsize::hedges_g(ai, hu)
  tibble(
    Measure = label,
    AI    = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(ai), sd(ai)),
    Human = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(hu), sd(hu)),
    t     = round(unname(tt$statistic), 2),
    df    = round(unname(tt$parameter), 1),
    p     = formatP(tt$p.value),
    g     = round(g$Hedges_g, 2)
  )
})
knitr::kable(auditTab,
  caption = "Table 8. Counterpart text by Label: two register features the enforcement pipeline did not control. AI and Human columns show M (SD); Welch's t. Em-dash rate was 0 in both cells (Step-1 strip confirmed, §1c).")
```
## 4f. Extended register features and stylometric classifier by Label

The §4e test compared two features. Five more extend it, and a classifier asks the sharper question: whether the assigned Label is predictable from the text at all. Trained on the seven surface features, an AUC near 0.50 with a non-significant permutation test is what register-constancy predicts, and it licenses reading trust as a response to conduct held identical across conditions. The test is between-condition and surface. It cannot establish that the text read as human, which §1c and the limitations leave open.

```{r register-extended-by-label}
extMeasures <- c(
  fnWordRatio = "Function-word ratio",
  meanWordLen = "Mean word length (characters)",
  sentLenSD   = "Message-length SD (words)",
  hapaxRatio  = "Hapax ratio (once-only words)",
  punctPer100 = "Punctuation per 100 words"
)
extTab <- imap_dfr(extMeasures, function(lab, var) {
  if (!var %in% names(data)) return(NULL)
  dd <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[var]]))
  ai <- dd %>% filter(Label == "AI")    %>% pull(.data[[var]])
  hu <- dd %>% filter(Label == "Human") %>% pull(.data[[var]])
  if (length(ai) < 2 || length(hu) < 2 || sd(c(ai, hu)) == 0) return(NULL)
  tt <- tryCatch(t.test(ai, hu), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(tt)) return(NULL)
  g  <- effectsize::hedges_g(ai, hu)
  tibble(
    Measure = lab,
    AI    = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(ai), sd(ai)),
    Human = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(hu), sd(hu)),
    t     = round(unname(tt$statistic), 2),
    df    = round(unname(tt$parameter), 1),
    p     = formatP(tt$p.value),
    g     = round(g$Hedges_g, 2)
  )
})
knitr::kable(extTab,
  caption = "Table 9. Extended register features by Label. AI and Human columns show M (SD); Welch's t. Surface features only; a null supports register-constancy across the label.")
```

```{r register-classifier}
set.seed(cfg$seed)
featCols <- c("wordsPerMsg", "ttr", "fnWordRatio", "meanWordLen",
              "sentLenSD", "hapaxRatio", "punctPer100")
featCols <- featCols[featCols %in% names(data)]

clfDat <- data %>%
  select(Label, all_of(featCols)) %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(featCols), ~ !is.na(.)))

# drop near-constant columns (a zero-variance predictor breaks glm)
keepCols <- featCols[vapply(featCols,
             function(v) sd(clfDat[[v]]) > 1e-8, logical(1))]
X <- scale(as.matrix(clfDat[, keepCols]))
y <- as.integer(clfDat$Label == "AI")

# leave-one-out CV logistic regression
looPred <- numeric(length(y))
for (i in seq_along(y)) {
  fit <- suppressWarnings(glm(y[-i] ~ X[-i, ], family = binomial()))
  looPred[i] <- as.numeric(plogis(cbind(1, X[i, , drop = FALSE]) %*% coef(fit)))
}
aucFun <- function(pred, lab) {
  pos <- pred[lab == 1]; neg <- pred[lab == 0]
  if (!length(pos) || !length(neg)) return(NA_real_)
  mean(outer(pos, neg, ">") + 0.5 * outer(pos, neg, "=="))
}
aucObs <- aucFun(looPred, y)

# (1) LOO logistic permutation null, plus the shuffled-label mean AUC
set.seed(cfg$seed + 1)
permAuc  <- replicate(2000, aucFun(looPred, sample(y)))
aucP     <- mean(abs(permAuc - 0.5) >= abs(aucObs - 0.5))
permMean <- mean(permAuc)

# (2) Random forest, out-of-bag AUC (OOB votes, no in-sample leakage)
if (!requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("randomForest", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
set.seed(cfg$seed + 2)
rf     <- randomForest::randomForest(x = as.data.frame(X),
                                     y = factor(y), ntree = 2000)
aucRF  <- aucFun(rf$votes[, "1"], y)

# (3) Repeated 5-fold CV logistic AUC (10 repeats)
set.seed(cfg$seed + 3)
cvAUCs <- replicate(10, {
  folds <- sample(rep(seq_len(5), length.out = length(y)))
  pred  <- numeric(length(y))
  for (k in seq_len(5)) {
    tr <- folds != k; te <- folds == k
    f  <- suppressWarnings(glm(y[tr] ~ X[tr, ], family = binomial()))
    pred[te] <- as.numeric(plogis(cbind(1, X[te, , drop = FALSE]) %*% coef(f)))
  }
  aucFun(pred, y)
})
aucCV <- mean(cvAUCs)

# (4) Classifier-free distance permutation: Mahalanobis distance between the
#     AI and Human centroids in standardised feature space, vs a shuffled null
centDist <- function(lab) {
  d <- colMeans(X[lab == 1, , drop = FALSE]) - colMeans(X[lab == 0, , drop = FALSE])
  S <- cov(X) + diag(1e-8, ncol(X))
  sqrt(as.numeric(t(d) %*% solve(S) %*% d))
}
distObs  <- centDist(y)
set.seed(cfg$seed + 4)
permDist <- replicate(2000, centDist(sample(y)))
distP    <- mean(permDist >= distObs)

cat(sprintf("Stylometric label recovery from %d surface features (n = %d)\n",
            length(keepCols), length(y)))
cat(sprintf("  LOO-CV logistic AUC       = %.3f  (perm p = %s; shuffled mean = %.3f)\n",
            aucObs, formatP(aucP), permMean))
cat(sprintf("  Random forest OOB AUC     = %.3f\n", aucRF))
cat(sprintf("  Repeated 5-fold CV AUC    = %.3f\n", aucCV))
cat(sprintf("  Mahalanobis centroid dist = %.3f  (perm p = %s)\n", distObs, formatP(distP)))
cat(sprintf("  Read: AUC near 0.50 with a null permutation would indicate register-constancy.\n"))

clfSummary <- tibble::tibble(
  Method        = c("LOO-CV logistic", "Random forest (OOB)",
                    "Repeated 5-fold CV logistic", "Mahalanobis centroid distance"),
  Statistic     = c("AUC", "AUC", "AUC", "distance"),
  Value         = round(c(aucObs, aucRF, aucCV, distObs), 3),
  `Perm. p`     = c(formatP(aucP), "", "", formatP(distP)),
  `Shuffled AUC`= c(round(permMean, 3), "", "", "")
)
knitr::kable(clfSummary,
  caption = "Table 31. Stylometric label recovery from the seven surface features (n = 200)")
```

# 6. Distributions (diagnostic)

```{r distributions, fig.height = 8}
distData <- data %>%
  select(Label, Transparency,
         trustMayer, competence, benevolence, predictability,
         openingDemand, finalDemand, concession,
         anthropomorphism, suspicion) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(Label, Transparency), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable,
    levels = c("trustMayer","competence","benevolence","predictability",
               "openingDemand","finalDemand","concession",
               "anthropomorphism","suspicion"),
    labels = c("Trust composite\n(1-5 Likert)",
               "Competence\n(1-5 Likert)",
               "Benevolence\n(1-5 Likert)",
               "Predictability\n(1-5 Likert)",
               "Opening demand\n(% equity)",
               "Final demand\n(% equity)",
               "Concession\n(percentage points)",
               "Anthropomorphism\n(1-5 scale)",
               "Suspicion\n(1-6 scale)"))) %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>% filter(any(!is.na(Value))) %>% ungroup()

# Means for vertical reference lines inside each panel
distMeans <- distData %>%
  drop_na(Value) %>%
  group_by(Variable, Label) %>%
  summarise(M = mean(Value), .groups = "drop")

discreteVars   <- "Suspicion\n(1-6 scale)"
distContinuous <- distData %>% filter(!Variable %in% discreteVars)
distDiscrete   <- distData %>% filter(Variable %in% discreteVars)

ggplot() +
  # Density curves for continuous variables
  geom_density(data = distContinuous,
               aes(Value, fill = Label, colour = Label),
               alpha = 0.30, linewidth = 0.6) +
  # Histogram bars for suspicion (discrete)
  geom_histogram(data = distDiscrete,
                 aes(Value, fill = Label, colour = Label,
                     y = after_stat(density)),
                 binwidth = 1, alpha = 0.40, position = "identity",
                 linewidth = 0.3) +
  # Mean reference lines — dashed vertical per condition
  geom_vline(data = distMeans,
             aes(xintercept = M, colour = Label),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Mean labels pinned to opposite top corners per panel (Human left, AI right)
  geom_text(data = distMeans %>%
              mutate(hjustVal = ifelse(Label == "Human", -0.15, 1.15),
                     xPos     = ifelse(Label == "Human", -Inf, Inf)),
            aes(x = xPos, y = Inf, label = sprintf("M = %.1f", M),
                colour = Label, hjust = hjustVal),
            vjust = 1.4, size = 2.7, fontface = "bold",
            show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Human = accentCol, AI = hlCol)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Human = accentCol, AI = hlCol)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density", fill = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold", lineheight = 1.1))

figText(
  "Distributions of primary measures by Label condition",
  "Density curves for continuous measures; histogram for suspicion")
```

# 7. Assumption checks

## 7a. Normality, variance, and multivariate normality

```{r assumptions}
shapTrust <- data %>%
  group_by(Label, Transparency) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(trustMayer)),
    W = if (n() >= 3 && sum(!is.na(trustMayer)) >= 3)
          shapiro.test(na.omit(trustMayer))$statistic else NA_real_,
    p = if (n() >= 3 && sum(!is.na(trustMayer)) >= 3)
          shapiro.test(na.omit(trustMayer))$p.value else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Normal = case_when(is.na(p) ~ "n < 3", p > .05 ~ "Yes", TRUE ~ "No"))
knitr::kable(roundDF(shapTrust),
             caption = "Table 11. Shapiro–Wilk on trust by cell")

levTrust  <- car::leveneTest(trustMayer    ~ Label * Transparency, data = data)
levDemand <- car::leveneTest(openingDemand ~ Label * Transparency, data = data)
cat(sprintf("\nLevene's test:\n  Trust:  F(%d, %d) = %.2f, p = %s\n  Demand: F(%d, %d) = %.2f, p = %s\n",
            levTrust$Df[1],  levTrust$Df[2],  levTrust$`F value`[1],  formatP(levTrust$`Pr(>F)`[1]),
            levDemand$Df[1], levDemand$Df[2], levDemand$`F value`[1], formatP(levDemand$`Pr(>F)`[1])))

mardia <- psych::mardia(data %>% select(competence, benevolence, predictability),
                        plot = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nMardia (MANOVA assumption): skew = %.2f, p = %s | kurt = %.2f, p = %s\n",
            mardia$b1p, formatP(mardia$p.skew), mardia$b2p, formatP(mardia$p.kurt)))
```

```{r qq-plot, fig.height = 4}
modAux <- aov(trustMayer ~ Label * Transparency, data = data)
resids <- residuals(modAux); qq <- qqnorm(resids, plot.it = FALSE)
qqDF <- tibble(theoretical = qq$x, sample = qq$y)
yq <- quantile(qqDF$sample, c(.25, .75)); xq <- qnorm(c(.25, .75))
slp <- diff(yq) / diff(xq); intc <- yq[1] - slp * xq[1]

ggplot(qqDF, aes(theoretical, sample)) +
  # Confidence envelope — shows where points should fall under normality
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, level = 0.95,
              colour = NA, fill = accentCol, alpha = 0.10) +
  # Reference line
  geom_abline(slope = slp, intercept = intc, colour = accentCol,
              linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  # Points coloured by how far they deviate from the line
  geom_point(aes(colour = abs(sample - (intc + slp * theoretical))),
             size = 2.2, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_colour_gradient(low = sigCol, high = nullCol,
                        name = "Deviation from\nnormality line") +
  # Shapiro-Wilk result as annotation
  annotate("text", x = min(qqDF$theoretical), y = max(qqDF$sample),
           label = sprintf("Shapiro-Wilk: W = %.3f, p = %s",
                           shapiro.test(resids)$statistic,
                           formatP(shapiro.test(resids)$p.value)),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.2, colour = mainCol, fontface = "italic") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles",
       title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) +
  theme(legend.key.height = unit(0.8, "cm"),
        legend.key.width  = unit(0.4, "cm"))

figText(
  "Residual quantile-quantile plot for the trust ANOVA",
  "Assessment of residual normality")
```

## 7b. Robust alternatives (if assumptions violated)

```{r robust-alternatives}
# Welch's ANOVA — does not assume equal variances across cells
welchTrust <- oneway.test(trustMayer ~ interaction(Label, Transparency), data = data)
cat(sprintf("Welch's ANOVA on trust: F(%.1f, %.1f) = %.2f, p = %s\n",
            welchTrust$parameter[1], welchTrust$parameter[2],
            welchTrust$statistic, formatP(welchTrust$p.value)))

# Kruskal-Wallis — non-parametric alternative
kwTrust <- kruskal.test(trustMayer ~ interaction(Label, Transparency), data = data)
cat(sprintf("Kruskal-Wallis on trust: H(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %s\n",
            kwTrust$parameter, kwTrust$statistic, formatP(kwTrust$p.value)))
```

## 7c. Outliers — studentised residuals (pre-registered ±3 rule)

```{r assumption-7c-outliers, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## Observations with studentised residuals exceeding ±3 in any ANCOVA model are flagged. 
## Primary models are reported with all observations included. If outliers are detected, a sensitivity analysis
## excluding them is reported alongside the primary results.

library(car)
candidate_dvs <- c("trustMayer", "openingDemand", "concession")
prereg_dvs <- candidate_dvs[candidate_dvs %in% names(data)]

row_id <- if ("participant.code" %in% names(data)) as.character(data$participant.code) else as.character(seq_len(nrow(data)))

flag_one <- function(dv) {
  m <- lm(addCovariates(as.formula(paste(dv, "~ Label * Transparency")), data), data = data)
  rst <- rstudent(m)
  used <- row_id[complete.cases(model.frame(m))]
  list(max_abs = max(abs(rst), na.rm = TRUE),
       n_over  = sum(abs(rst) > 3, na.rm = TRUE),
       out_ids = used[which(abs(rst) > 3)])
}
flags <- lapply(prereg_dvs, flag_one); names(flags) <- prereg_dvs

detect_tbl <- data.frame(
  Model = prereg_dvs,
  Max_abs_rstudent = round(sapply(flags, `[[`, "max_abs"), 3),
  N_over_3 = sapply(flags, `[[`, "n_over"),
  row.names = NULL
)

## save flagged IDs for the exclusion sensitivity run later (section 20)
outlier_ids <<- unique(unlist(lapply(flags, `[[`, "out_ids")))

cat("Studentised-residual outlier detection (|externally studentised r| > 3):\n")
print(detect_tbl, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nObservations flagged for the pre-registered exclusion sensitivity (reported in §20):",
    length(outlier_ids), "\n")
```


# 8. Power: planned target and achieved-N sensitivity curve

The pre-registered target is N ≈ 128 (G\*Power, *f* = 0.25, α = .05, 1 − β = .80) for the Label × Transparency interaction on trust (H3). The curve below shows the achievable power across plausible effect sizes for the realised N — post-data accompaniment to the planned analysis.

```{r power-curve, fig.height = 5}
# Effect-size grid is a visualization choice — not a formal test. The achieved N is marked with a vertical band, and the 80% power threshold is dashed.
if (!requireNamespace("ggrepel", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("ggrepel", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
fGrid <- c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.40)
nGrid <- seq(60, 320, by = 10)

powerDF <- expand_grid(f = fGrid, N = nGrid) %>%
  mutate(power = map2_dbl(f, N, \(f_, n_)
           pwr::pwr.f2.test(u = 1, v = n_ - 4, f2 = f_^2, sig.level = .05)$power),
         fLabel = factor(sprintf("f = %.2f", f)))

ggplot(powerDF, aes(N, power, colour = fLabel)) +
  # Power zone shading
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0.80, ymax = 1,
           fill = sigCol, alpha = 0.05) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = 0, ymax = 0.80,
           fill = nullCol, alpha = 0.03) +
  # Threshold line
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", colour = subtleCol, linewidth = 0.4) +
  # Achieved N — highlighted band
  annotate("rect", xmin = nrow(data) - 3, xmax = nrow(data) + 3,
           ymin = 0, ymax = 1, fill = hlCol, alpha = 0.12) +
  # Power curves
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  # Dots where each curve crosses the achieved N
  geom_point(data = powerDF %>% filter(N == nGrid[which.min(abs(nGrid - nrow(data)))]),
             size = 3.5, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1.2) +
  
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = powerDF %>% filter(N == max(nGrid), f >= 0.20),
    aes(label = fLabel, colour = fLabel), hjust = 0, size = 3, fontface = "bold",
    direction = "y", nudge_x = 14, min.segment.length = 0,
    segment.size = 0.4, box.padding = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +

  geom_text(
    data = powerDF %>% filter(N == max(nGrid), f < 0.20),
    aes(label = fLabel, colour = fLabel), hjust = -0.1, size = 3,
    fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Annotations
  annotate("text", x = max(nGrid), y = 0.12,
           label = paste0("Achieved N = ", nrow(data)),
           size = 3.5, colour = hlCol, fontface = "bold", hjust = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = max(nGrid), y = 0.83,
           label = "80% power threshold",
           hjust = 1, size = 2.8, colour = subtleCol, fontface = "italic") +
  # Scales
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                     labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4477AA","#66CCEE","#228833",
                                 "#CCBB44","#EE6677","#AA3377")) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Total sample size N", y = "Power",
       title = NULL, subtitle = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

figText(
  "Sensitivity power curve for the Label x Transparency interaction",
  "Power across effect sizes at the achieved sample size")
```

# CONFIRMATORY TESTS

# 9. H1 — AI label reduces trust

> **H1.** Participants in the AI-labelled condition report lower trust than those in the human-labelled condition. *Test*: main effect of Label in a 2×2 between-subjects ANOVA on the Mayer composite, adjusting for `suspicion` (Type-III SS).

```{r h1-trust}
modTrust <- aov(addCovariates(trustMayer ~ Label * Transparency, data),
                data = data)
trustTab <- tidyAnova3(modTrust)
knitr::kable(roundDF(trustTab, 3),
             caption = "Table 12. H1 / H3 — Trust ANOVA (Type-III SS, covariate-adjusted)")

emmTrust <- emmeans(modTrust, ~ Label * Transparency)
print(emmTrust)
cat("\nSimple effects of Label within each Transparency level:\n")
print(contrast(emmTrust, "pairwise", by = "Transparency", adjust = "tukey"))

gTrust <- effectsize::hedges_g(trustMayer ~ Label, data = data)
cat(sprintf("\nLabel main effect: Hedges' g = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]\n",
            gTrust$Hedges_g, gTrust$CI_low, gTrust$CI_high))
```

## 9b. Did the label move BELIEF (not just recall)?

```{r belief-decomposition}
beliefSplit <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(suspicion)) %>%
  mutate(believesAI = suspicion >= 4) %>%
  group_by(Label) %>%
  summarise(n             = n(),
            meanSuspicion = mean(suspicion),
            sdSuspicion   = sd(suspicion),
            nBelievesAI   = sum(believesAI),
            pctBelievesAI = mean(believesAI) * 100,
            .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(roundDF(beliefSplit, 2),
  caption = "Table 13. Belief by Label condition — mean suspicion and % believing the partner was AI")

beliefT <- t.test(suspicion ~ Label, data = data %>% filter(!is.na(suspicion)))
cat(sprintf("\nBelief (suspicion 1-6) by Label: Welch t(%.1f) = %.2f, p = %s\n",
            beliefT$parameter, beliefT$statistic, formatP(beliefT$p.value)))

beliefChi <- data %>% filter(!is.na(suspicion)) %>%
  mutate(believesAI = suspicion >= 4) %>%
  {suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table(.$Label, .$believesAI)))}
cat(sprintf("%% believing AI by Label: chi-sq(%.0f) = %.2f, p = %s | AI cond = %.1f%%, Human cond = %.1f%%\n",
            beliefChi$parameter, beliefChi$statistic, formatP(beliefChi$p.value),
            beliefSplit$pctBelievesAI[beliefSplit$Label == "AI"],
            beliefSplit$pctBelievesAI[beliefSplit$Label == "Human"]))
```

## 9c. Trust tracks BELIEF (continuous suspicion) — the registered covariate

```{r suspicion-trust-association}
## Exploratory (not pre-registered). Suspicion is the pre-registered continuous covariate; 
## the belief bands (1-2 human, 3-4 ambivalent, 5-6 convinced AI) are post-hoc groupings used for description only.
suspTrust <- data %>% filter(!is.na(trustMayer), !is.na(suspicion))

# Registered continuous treatment: trust on suspicion (1-6), adjusted for factors
modSuspTrust <- lm(trustMayer ~ suspicion + Label + Transparency, data = suspTrust)
bF   <- coef(modSuspTrust)["suspicion"]
ciF  <- confint(modSuspTrust)["suspicion", ]
pF   <- summary(modSuspTrust)$coefficients["suspicion", "Pr(>|t|)"]
betaF <- bF * sd(suspTrust$suspicion) / sd(suspTrust$trustMayer)
cat(sprintf("Continuous (1-6, n=%d): b = %.3f [%.3f, %.3f], beta = %.3f, p = %s\n",
            nrow(suspTrust), bF, ciF[1], ciF[2], betaF, formatP(pF)))

# Is it linear or concentrated? Quadratic term test
modQuad <- lm(trustMayer ~ suspicion + I(suspicion^2) + Label + Transparency, data = suspTrust)
pQuad <- summary(modQuad)$coefficients["I(suspicion^2)", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Quadratic term: p = %s (ns => globally ~linear; see band slopes below)\n", formatP(pQuad)))

# Per-point trust means — shows where the drop actually starts
pointMeans <- suspTrust %>%
  group_by(suspicion) %>%
  summarise(trustM = mean(trustMayer), trustSD = sd(trustMayer), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(roundDF(pointMeans, 2),
  caption = "Table 14. Trust at each suspicion point (1 = Definitely human ... 6 = Definitely AI)")

# Band slopes: ambivalent middle (3-4) vs convinced AI (5-6)
runBand <- function(df, lab) {
  rho <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(df$trustMayer, df$suspicion, method = "spearman"))
  cat(sprintf("%s (n=%d): Spearman rho = %.3f, p = %s\n",
              lab, nrow(df), rho$estimate, formatP(rho$p.value)))
}
runBand(suspTrust %>% filter(suspicion %in% c(3, 4)), "Ambivalent (susp 3-4)")
runBand(suspTrust %>% filter(suspicion >= 5),         "Convinced AI (susp 5-6)")

# Strict believed-AI (>=5) adjusted slope — the convinced-only association
strictAI <- suspTrust %>% filter(suspicion >= 5)
modStrict <- lm(trustMayer ~ suspicion + Label + Transparency, data = strictAI)
bS <- coef(modStrict)["suspicion"]; ciS <- confint(modStrict)["suspicion", ]
pS <- summary(modStrict)$coefficients["suspicion", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Convinced-AI strict (>=5, n=%d): b = %.3f [%.3f, %.3f], p = %s\n",
            nrow(strictAI), bS, ciS[1], ciS[2], formatP(pS)))

# >=4 version reported alongside, so the dilution from including "Probably AI" is visible
broadAI <- suspTrust %>% filter(suspicion >= 4)
modBroad <- lm(trustMayer ~ suspicion + Label + Transparency, data = broadAI)
bB <- coef(modBroad)["suspicion"]; pB <- summary(modBroad)$coefficients["suspicion", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat(sprintf("Believed-AI broad (>=4, incl. 'Probably AI', n=%d): b = %.3f, p = %s\n",
            nrow(broadAI), bB, formatP(pB)))
```

## 9e. Overall trust — pre-registered single-item convergent check

```{r overall-trust-check}
# Pre-registered confirmatory single-item check on the Mayer composite.
# Item: "Overall, how much did you trust Volo Technologies' representative
# during the negotiation?" (1-7). Registered as a convergent check
# alongside trustMayer.

# (a) Convergent validity: does the single item track the composite?
overallTrustCor <- cor.test(data$overallTrust, data$trustMayer,
                            use = "complete.obs")
cat(sprintf(
  "Single-item overall trust vs Mayer composite: r = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f], p %s (n = %d)\n",
  overallTrustCor$estimate,
  overallTrustCor$conf.int[1], overallTrustCor$conf.int[2],
  ifelse(overallTrustCor$p.value < .001, "< .001",
         sprintf("= %.3f", overallTrustCor$p.value)),
  sum(!is.na(data$overallTrust) & !is.na(data$trustMayer))))

# (b) Does the label move the single item, as it did not move the composite?
modOverall  <- aov(addCovariates(overallTrust ~ Label * Transparency, data),
                   data = data)
overallTab  <- tidyAnova3(modOverall)
knitr::kable(roundDF(overallTab, 3),
             caption = "Table 15. Overall trust (single item, 1-7) — Type-III SS, covariate-adjusted")

# (c) Effect size for the Label main effect, to sit beside the composite's g
gOverall <- effectsize::hedges_g(overallTrust ~ Label, data = data)
cat(sprintf("\nLabel main effect on overall trust: Hedges' g = %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]\n",
            gOverall$Hedges_g, gOverall$CI_low, gOverall$CI_high))
```

# 10. H2a — Transparency raises opening demands

> **H2a.** Participants in the transparent condition make higher opening demands. *Test*: main effect of Transparency on `openingDemand` in a covariate-adjusted 2×2 ANOVA.

```{r h2a-opening}
modOpen <- aov(addCovariates(openingDemand ~ Label * Transparency, data),
               data = data)
openTab <- tidyAnova3(modOpen)
knitr::kable(roundDF(openTab, 3),
             caption = "Table 16. H2a — Opening-demand ANOVA (Type-III SS, covariate-adjusted)")

emmOpen <- emmeans(modOpen, ~ Label * Transparency)
print(contrast(emmOpen, "pairwise", by = "Label", adjust = "tukey"))
```

# 11. H2b — Transparency yields smaller cumulative concessions

> **H2b.** Transparent participants concede less across rounds. *Test*: main effect of Transparency on `concession` (= openingDemand − finalDemand) in a covariate-adjusted 2×2 ANOVA. The mixed-effects model below provides a complementary view by modelling the demand × round interaction directly.

## 11a. Concession ANOVA (primary H2b test)

```{r h2b-concession}
modConcession <- aov(addCovariates(concession ~ Label * Transparency, data),
                     data = data)
concessionTab <- tidyAnova3(modConcession)
knitr::kable(roundDF(concessionTab, 3),
             caption = "Table 17. H2b — Concession ANOVA (Type-III SS, covariate-adjusted)")
```

## 11b. Round-level mixed-effects model on demand

```{r h2-mixed}
# Covariate-aware mixed model. addCovariates() doesn't carry random effects,
# so we build the formula manually. Only covariates that are present and non-constant in this export are included.
useCovs <- cfg$covariates[
  vapply(cfg$covariates, \(v)
         v %in% names(dataLong) &&
         sum(!is.na(dataLong[[v]])) >= cfg$covariate_min_nonNA &&
         length(unique(na.omit(dataLong[[v]]))) >= cfg$covariate_min_distinct,
         logical(1))
]
fixedRHS     <- paste(c("Label * Transparency * round", useCovs), collapse = " + ")
mixedFormula <- as.formula(paste0("demand ~ ", fixedRHS, " + (1 | participantCode)"))

if (length(useCovs) < length(cfg$covariates)) {
  message("Mixed model: dropped ",
          paste(setdiff(cfg$covariates, useCovs), collapse = ", "),
          " (all-NA or constant in this export).")
}

modDemand <- lmer(mixedFormula, data = dataLong)
print(parameters::parameters(modDemand, ci_method = "satterthwaite"))
print(anova(modDemand, type = "III"))
print(performance::r2(modDemand))
```

## 11c. Demand trajectory (publication figure)

```{r h2-trajectory, fig.height = 5}
trajData <- dataLong %>%
  group_by(Label, Transparency, round) %>%
  summarise(M = mean(demand, na.rm = TRUE),
            SE = sd(demand, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(Cell = factor(paste(Label, Transparency, sep = "—"),
                       levels = c("Human—Opaque","Human—Transparent",
                                  "AI—Opaque","AI—Transparent")))

ggplot(trajData, aes(round, M, colour = Cell, fill = Cell)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = M - SE, ymax = M + SE), alpha = 0.18, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(palette4)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = unname(palette4)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_len(cfg$n_rounds)) +
  labs(x = "Negotiation round", y = "Mean equity demand (%)",
       colour = "Condition", fill = "Condition",
       title = NULL, subtitle = NULL)

figText(
  "Mean equity demand across negotiation rounds by condition",
  "Demand trajectories for the four experimental cells")
```
